# The exit-contract activation dossier — `mx_btcusd @ target_5R` and `sub_xvol_pullback @ target_4R`

**Session AS, blocks B1520–B1539.** Generated by
`phase11/receipts/as_activation_dossier.py` from
`phase11/receipts/AS_EXIT_CONTRACT_ACTIVATION_V1.json`; every figure is read out of that
artifact and none is transcribed.

These are the next two live changes and **they are CONTRACT changes, not tag changes.** The
five-sleeve expansion moved a string in a launch command and no config byte; these move Python
that decides where a broker take-profit is placed. This page arms nothing. It says exactly what
each change is, what it costs, what it cannot break, and — for one of the two — that it is not
ready to be proposed.

---

## 0. The finding that governs both changes

**Editing `final_target_r` in `SLEEVE_EXIT_PROFILES` is a NO-OP for the entire `mx_*` cohort,**
and an activation package that did only that would arm `mx_btcusd` on the 2R contract its own
evidence REJECTS at every band — while **the spec, the diff and the commit message all said
5R**.

> **Corrected after an adversarial pass.** A first cut of this page said *"every log would say
> 5R"*, and that is false and matters: the runtime logs read the **resolved** value, so they
> would correctly say 2.0. The deception is in the *source*, not in the telemetry — which is
> better news for anyone watching a live book and worse news for anyone reviewing a diff.

The mechanism: execution_packets.py:249-256 — when `final_from_intent` is truthy and the intent supplies positive target_dist and stop_dist, final_target_r is native_target/native_stop and the profile's own final_target_r at :260 is never reached.

Proved behaviourally by driving the real `build_book_trade_params` under three profile states:

| profile state | resolved `final_target_r` | broker TP on a 100,000 entry with a 1,000 stop |
|---|---:|---:|
| as committed (`final_target_r=2.0`, `final_from_intent=True`) | 2.0 | 102,000 |
| **the naive edit**: `final_target_r=5.0` | 2.0 | 102,000 |
| `final_target_r=5.0` **and** `final_from_intent` removed | 5.0 | 105,000 |
| generator route: `market_expansion_d1.TARGET_R = 5.0` | 5.0 | 105,000 |

`sub_xvol_pullback` is not exposed to this: its profile carries no `final_from_intent`, so the
same edit resolves as written — 3.0 → 4.0.

> an activation package that lands `final_target_r=5.0` alone would arm the sleeve on the 2R contract its own evidence REJECTS at every band, while every log and every spec read would say 5R. This is the single most expensive thing on this page.

(The artifact's `consequence` field carries the same first-cut phrasing about logs; the
correction above governs.)

## 1. `mx_btcusd @ target_5R` — the exact spec diff

**Two routes reach the 5R contract, and they are not equivalent.**

### Route A — the profile route (RECOMMENDED)

```python
# src/components/ultimate_book/execution_packets.py
# after the MARKET_EXPANSION_TARGET2_SLEEVES block that sets the cohort default:
SLEEVE_EXIT_PROFILES["mx_btcusd_d1_donchian_20_breakout"] = dict(
    policy="time_stop",
    final_target_r=5.0,          # the admission's own cell
    #  NO `final_from_intent` — with it the generator's 2R wins and this line is dead
    time_stop_bars=time_stop_m15(RESEARCH_HORIZON_NATIVE_BARS, "D1"),   # 7680, unchanged
)
```

**Blast radius, measured** by resolving all 34 registered sleeves'
exit fields before and after, through **both** production resolvers: **1 sleeve moves**, it is the one named, and
**0 armed sleeves move.** Change class
`DEFAULT_OFF_SLEEVE_ONLY`.

> **There are TWO resolvers and only one honours `final_from_intent`.** `build_book_trade_params` (`:249-256`) does; `native_policy_instrumentation` (`:152-181`, the
> adopt-missing-record rehydration path) reads `final_target_r` at `:165-166` **unguarded**. So
> under the *naive* edit the two DISAGREE — 2R at the broker, 5R in the rehydration payload,
> which `book_owner.py:2724` persists. That divergence used to be inert because the hydrator
> raised `KeyError('trigger_r')` before reaching the broker; **this session fixed that (B1535),
> so it is now reachable.** Route A is the recommendation partly for this reason: dropping
> `final_from_intent` is the only form of the change under which both resolvers carry the same
> number. Pinned by three tests. A first cut of this dossier measured the blast radius through
> one resolver only — an adversarial pass found it.

### Route B — the generator route (NOT recommended)

Changing `market_expansion_d1.TARGET_R` from 2.0 to 5.0 also produces a
5R contract — but `TARGET_R` is a **module constant shared by every `mx_*` generator**, so it
moves **14 sleeves**, not one. It cannot be scoped to
`mx_btcusd` without a further code change. Route A is one dict entry with a blast radius of one.

### What does NOT change

`time_stop_bars` stays at 7680 — AQ's repair, landed at B1404. **The admission is a property of
both changes together**: at mid band, the time-stop repair alone gives p 0.0064 (REJECT), the 5R
target alone under the old one-bar stop gives p 0.0564 (REJECT), and both together give
p 0.0011 (ADMIT). Any package citing this cell must name the repair as well as the target.

## 2. `sub_xvol_pullback @ target_4R` — and why this one is NOT ready

This is a change to an **ARMED** sleeve's live contract. Two things have to be said before the
diff, and the second one is why the change is not proposed today.

### 2a. The headline figure is widely misread, including in this session's own commission

> AK's `target_4R` pooled_oos_mean_r is 1.1565 R/day and `as_walked` is 1.0264. The CHANGE is +0.130 R/day, not +1.157 — the larger figure is the LEVEL of the cell, and reading it as the improvement overstates the change 8.9x.

### 2b. AK measured this cell at a standard that does not govern the estate — so it was re-gated

AK's frontier carries **no population key and no `spread_band` key**, which means ALL_ERAS at the
flat 37-day snapshot, at the historical 69-look family. The estate's ratified standard is
**RECORDED, banded, at `CANDIDATE_BOOK_V1`**. This session ran that.

**Control first**: AK's published cell reproduces here to the digit at ALL_ERAS / flat —
R/day 1.1564749459, p
0.0077992201. `r_per_day_reproduces`
**True**, `p_reproduces` **True**. So any difference
below is the standard, not the instrument.

| population | band | `as_walked` (= the live 3R contract) | `target_4R` | Δ | verdict | p_raw | q at family 48 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| RECORDED | flat *(control)* | 1.0036 | 1.3471 | **+0.3435** | REJECT | 0.007999 | 0.3840 |
| RECORDED | low | 1.0273 | 1.3708 | **+0.3435** | REJECT | 0.007999 | 0.3840 |
| RECORDED | mid | 1.0215 | 1.3651 | **+0.3435** | REJECT | 0.007999 | 0.3840 |
| RECORDED | high | 1.0129 | 1.3565 | **+0.3435** | REJECT | 0.007999 | 0.3840 |
| ALL_ERAS | flat *(control)* | 1.0264 | 1.1565 | **+0.1301** | REJECT | 0.007799 | 0.3744 |
| ALL_ERAS | low | 1.0495 | 1.1795 | **+0.1301** | REJECT | 0.007699 | 0.3696 |
| ALL_ERAS | mid | 1.0438 | 1.1739 | **+0.1301** | REJECT | 0.007699 | 0.3696 |
| ALL_ERAS | high | 1.0356 | 1.1657 | **+0.1301** | REJECT | 0.007799 | 0.3744 |

**Three things that table says, in order of how much they matter:**

1. **The change is worth MORE at the ratified rule, not less.** +0.3435 R/day on RECORDED against +0.1301 on ALL_ERAS — 2.6×. The delta is identical across all four bands, which is expected and is a check: the band charges spread, both arms hold the same entries, so the spread term cancels in the difference.

2. **`as_walked` and the sleeve's declared 3R target are the SAME arm to the digit** (1.0215 R/day, p 0.011999). That is a live-contract fidelity confirmation worth having on an armed sleeve: the walk's baseline IS what the book runs.

3. **It still REJECTS at every band.** REJECT significance: q=0.384 (raw p=0.007999) fails benjamini_hochberg at alpha=0.1 across a family of 48 The raw p is 0.007999 against a BH rank-1 bar of 0.002083 — **3.8× ABOVE it**, not a near miss.

### 2c. The change also buys carry, and this sleeve's largest cost term is swap

| | `as_walked` | `target_4R` |
|---|---:|---:|
| mean swap nights | 4.2692 | 6.4615 |
| median hold (h) | 92.0 | 123.0 |
| swap share of cost | 0.543 | 0.648 |

a wider target is a LONGER hold, and this sleeve's largest cost term is swap. The change buys R/day and spends carry, and its carry tier was computed at the shorter hold.

### 2d. The maxbars share, declared — on the POPULATION-FILTERED rows

The wave-12 delta: an exit sweep that does not report its truncation share is quoting a
frontier it has not priced. At the ratified rule (RECORDED):

| cell | maxbars / n | share | share on the pre-population set |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `as_walked` | 4 / 85 | 0.0471 | 0.0455 |
| `target_4R` | 7 / 85 | 0.0824 | 0.0909 |

> A first cut of this driver stamped the **pre-population** row set onto every arm, so each
> RECORDED arm reported `n: 88` beside `n_trades: 85`. Caught by an adversarial pass; the
> numbers above are the filtered ones and both are published so the difference is visible.

**And the population attribution, stated because the +0.3435 rests on it.** `RECORDED` drops
exactly **3 of the 88** trades, and here they are:

| symbol | entry | `r_gross` | exit |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `US500.cash` | 2021-07-08 | +3.0000 | target |
| `JP225.cash` | 2023-03-10 | −1.0000 | stop |
| `XAUEUR` | 2023-03-21 | +3.0000 | target |

Two of the three are **+3R target hits under the native contract** — precisely the trades whose
behaviour a 4R target changes. So the amplification of the delta from +0.1301 to +0.3435 rests
on three excluded trades out of 88, and this session did **not** run the per-trade attribution.
The three are named so that anyone can. On a REJECT that changes nothing; on an admission it
would have to be run first.

### 2e. The diff, for when it is ready

```python
# src/components/ultimate_book/execution_packets.py:84
-"sub_xvol_pullback": dict(policy="time_stop", final_target_r=3.0,  time_stop_bars=1280),
+"sub_xvol_pullback": dict(policy="time_stop", final_target_r=4.0,  time_stop_bars=1280),
```

**Blast radius, measured: 1 sleeve moves and it is the one named.** But
`armed_sleeves_moved` is `['sub_xvol_pullback']` and the change class is
**`CHANGES_AN_ARMED_SLEEVES_LIVE_CONTRACT`** — that is not a defect, it is the entire reason this needs an owner
decision rather than a merge.

> **RECOMMENDATION: do not propose this change yet.** It is a REJECT at the ratified rule at
> every band, 3.8× outside the rank-1 bar, on an armed sleeve, and it increases carry on the
> sleeve whose cost is 54–65 % swap. The +0.3435 R/day is real and it is worth re-visiting when
> the sample supports it — `n` is 85 on RECORDED with 3 evaluable folds. What would change the
> answer is sample, not a repair on this axis.

## 3. Seal membership — the H1/R2 answer, across all three mechanisms

CLAUDE.md is explicit that H1's input-binding drift check does NOT catch a worktree-local flip (the runner's binding_roots fallback ends at MAIN_REPO_ROOT); the seal breaks via config_file_hashes -> shared_execution_contract_digest_sha256. Cite the execution-seal digest, not the drift check. `code_authority_paths` is the third: it binds files a SECOND time from inside an executing file.

| file | R2 `input_bindings` | R1 `input_bindings` | `code_authority_paths` (21 entries) | `config_file_hashes` | **sealed?** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `src/components/ultimate_book/execution_packets.py` | — | — | — | — | unbound |
| `src/components/ultimate_book/sleeves/market_expansion_d1.py` | — | — | — | — | unbound |
| `src/components/ultimate_book/admission.py` | — | — | — | — | unbound |
| `src/components/ultimate_book/sleeves/candidate_registry.py` | — | — | — | — | unbound |
| `config/agent_config.yaml` | common_behavior_inputs | common_behavior_inputs | — | YES | **SEALED** |
| `config/profiles/operator_profile.yaml` | common_behavior_inputs | common_behavior_inputs | — | YES | **SEALED** |
| `config/profiles/redacted_account.yaml` | — | — | — | — | unbound |
| `src/components/exit_policy_v4.py` | common_behavior_inputs | common_behavior_inputs | YES | — | **SEALED** |

> **The answer, plainly: NEITHER change ends the parked B7.5 campaign option.**
> `execution_packets.py` and `market_expansion_d1.py` are bound by **none** of the three
> mechanisms — not R2's 43 input bindings, not the runner's
> 21 `code_authority_paths`, and not the two files in
> `config_file_hashes` that feed `shared_execution_contract_digest_sha256`. There is no owner
> question to route here.

For contrast, and because these are the files a careless diff would reach for: `config/agent_config.yaml`, `config/profiles/operator_profile.yaml` and `src/components/exit_policy_v4.py` **are** sealed, each by two or three mechanisms. `config/profiles/redacted_account.yaml` is bound by neither contract — but it carries live authority and the redacted_account token binds its bytes, so it is untouchable for a different reason.

## 4. Token implications

**NO token implication for either change. The token binds the CONFIG digest; SLEEVE_EXIT_PROFILES and market_expansion_d1.TARGET_R are Python source, not config. Neither change moves a byte of config/agent_config.yaml or either profile, so neither invalidates a minted token and neither needs a re-mint.**

Verified: the config-digest call sites above are the only consumers; none reads a source file. The FIVE_SLEEVE ceremony is the precedent: it changed --tags on both hosts and the receipt records the SAME digests the tokens bind.

**But:** a source change still requires a HOST DEPLOY (the carry ceremony), because the VPS runs its own tree. That is the orchestrator's, and it is where the real risk of these changes lives — not in the token.

## 5. Test plan

Per change, and none of it needs market data:

| # | test | what it pins |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | drive `build_book_trade_params` for the changed sleeve and assert the resolved `final_target_r` **and** `take_profit_1` | that the edit is not a no-op — the single failure mode this dossier exists to prevent |
| 2 | assert `final_from_intent` is absent from the changed `mx_btcusd` profile, by name | that a later edit cannot silently re-introduce the no-op |
| 3 | blast-radius snapshot: resolve every registered sleeve before and after and assert exactly the named sleeve moved | that the change has no unnamed reach |
| 4 | assert every ARMED sleeve's resolved params are byte-identical across the change (for `mx_btcusd`) | that live money does not move |
| 5 | assert the three fail-closed live gates still pass for the changed sleeve (`.tools/probe_per_sleeve_exit_gates.py` is the precedent) | that the packet is still placeable |
| 6 | a coverage test that fails if a sleeve is added without a snapshot row | that test 3 cannot silently stop covering the registry — AQ's `test_time_stop_units.py` pattern |

`tests/ultimate_book/test_exit_contract_activation.py` in this session implements 1–4 and 6 against BOTH candidate diffs, applied in memory — so the tests exist and pass **before** any spec byte moves, which is the only order in which test 1 can prove anything.

## 6. Rollback

| | `mx_btcusd` | `sub_xvol_pullback` |
|---|---|---|
| **revert** | delete the added `SLEEVE_EXIT_PROFILES[...]` entry; the cohort comprehension at `:144-148` restores the 2R/`final_from_intent` default | restore `final_target_r=3.0` |
| **blast radius of the revert** | 1 sleeve, 0 armed | 1 sleeve, 1 armed |
| **token** | none — no config byte moves either way | none |
| **seal** | none — the file is unbound by all three mechanisms | none |
| **open positions** | a position opened under 5R keeps the **broker-side TP set at entry** (`execution.py:3488`), so a revert does not move an open trade's target — it changes the next entry only | same |
| **host** | the revert is a deploy, i.e. the carry ceremony again. Reverting in this repo alone changes nothing live. | same |

> The asymmetry worth naming: **landing is a deploy and reverting is a deploy.** Neither change
> can be undone by flipping a flag, because there is no flag — the contract is code. If a
> reversible form is wanted, that is a different design (a config-keyed target), and it would
> put the value in a file that IS sealed and IS token-bound. The unbound-code form is the
> cheaper one and this dossier recommends it.

Cell: `mx_btcusd_d1_donchian_20_breakout` @ `target_5R`, population `RECORDED`, band `mid`, option `B_balanced` — verdict **ADMIT**, p_raw 0.0010998900. Fold rule `equal_calendar_folds_over_sleeve_span`.

| fold | OOS window | n | disputed | gross R/trade | **fold R/day** |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 2019-01-03 … 2020-05-07 | 36 | 15 | 1.3333 | 1.1341 |
| 2 | 2020-05-08 … 2021-09-11 | 42 | 38 | 1.8046 | 1.5118 |
| 3 | 2021-09-12 … 2023-01-16 | 26 | 0 | 2.1458 | 1.8663 |

> 0.9817.** The recent two folds average
> 0.1981 against the first three's
> 1.5041 — **13.2%**, on
> 80 of 184 OOS trades and the most
> recent 2.7 years. Every gate passes anyway, because `stability` counts the **sign** of a fold
> mean and not its level, so a 7.6× chronological decay reads as 5/5 positive by construction.

**And the bill has moved since the admission was ratified.** p is family-invariant; only the bar
moves:

| declared family | size | BH rank-1 bar at α = 0.10 | p is inside by |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| V3, at ratification | 39 | 0.0025641 | 2.33× |
| **V5, now** | **48** | 0.0020833 | **1.89×** |

**Still admits at the current family: True.** The wave-11 ratchet raised
`CANDIDATE_BOOK_V1` from 39 to 48 and the admission survives it, with less headroom.

## 8. What each change still needs before it reaches the owner

**`mx_btcusd @ target_5R` — one hard precondition, and it is not a research question.**
After AQ's time-stop repair an open `mx_*` position requests **7,744** M15 bars per tick. If the
terminal returns fewer than 7,680 closed M15 bars, the printed-bar count can never reach the
budget and **the time stop never fires at all** — the wall-clock fallback does not catch it,
because that path needs a `None` return and not an honestly short count. The backstop degrades to
**inert**, not late. Nothing armed is exposed today (the five live sleeves are H4 at 1280, want
1344). **Measure the terminal's `copy_rates` ceiling before arming anything in this cohort** —
it is `F15` on the fleet map, the cheapest item there, and it is a precondition rather than a
nice-to-have.

Beyond that: registry confidence is 0.025, so admitting the sleeve into the funded book is
**economically inert** (~0.136 %/month) — re-weighting is a separate owner decision (OD-AI-5),
and the eligibility-vs-allocation distinction in `MX_BTCUSD_CHALLENGE_DOSSIER.md` §6 stands.

**`sub_xvol_pullback @ target_4R` — sample.** It is a REJECT at every band at the ratified rule,
3.8× outside the rank-1 bar, on 85 trades and 3 evaluable folds. Nothing about the change is
wrong; there is simply not enough of it. Re-visit when `n` supports it, and until then the armed
sleeve keeps the 3R contract its own walk baseline reproduces exactly.
